what is compost # “mixture of ingredients used as plant fertilizer and to improve soil’s physical, chemical, and biological properties” - wikipedia
why we compost # improve soil health and fertility (increases nutrient content and biodiversity of microbes) reduce dependence on chemical fertilisers reduce waste in landfills (plant waste, food waste) ingredients (have been told it’s like baking a cake!) # - carbon # needed for energy; the microbial oxidation of carbon produces the heat required for other parts of the composting process. high carbon materials tend to be brown and dry.
nearly all dead plant and animal materials have both carbon and nitrogen in different amounts.
high carbon things # - nitrogen # needed to grow and reproduce more organisms to oxidize the carbon. high nitrogen materials tend to be green and wet or colourful!
- oxygen # - water # what goes in? # basically anything organic (which basically means derived from living things!)
plant waste (cuttings) animal waste (sadly, not so much at kwf) food waste coffee grounds (use sparingly, acidic) compost friends! # earthworms black soldier flies flies ants snails slugs sources:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compost https://www.rhs.org.uk/soil-composts-mulches/what-is-organic-matter
